author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Higher gasoline costs are expected to push the U.S. consumer price index up more quickly in August, making Friday’s inflation report an important input for markets ahead of the Federal Reserve’s next policy meeting.

Economists surveyed by Reuters forecast a 0.4% monthly increase in the headline CPI and a 3.4% rise from a year earlier. Core prices, which exclude food and energy, are expected to increase 0.2% for the month. Those figures are forecasts, not released results.

The Energy Information Administration reported that average gasoline prices rose to $4.192 per gallon in August from $4.064 in July. Fuel can affect the headline index directly and also influence transportation and distribution costs across the economy.

Investors will compare the official data with expectations to reassess the likely path of interest rates. A reading above forecast could reinforce concern that energy pressures are spreading, while a softer result could ease some of those fears. The Federal Reserve meets next week, giving the report unusual weight even though policymakers typically examine several inflation and labor indicators rather than one month in isolation.
dek: Economists surveyed by Reuters forecast a 0.4% monthly CPI increase, with Friday’s report likely to shape expectations before the Federal Reserve meets.
headline: Gasoline expected to lift August U.S. inflation reading
